meta.title_plain: How a young ski champion became tennis world No. 1
meta.teaser: Jannik Sinner raced down mountains, then picked tennis and reached No. 1.

page.title: How a ski champion from the mountains became tennis world No. 1
page.bigIdea: Jannik Sinner was great at skiing, but he chose tennis. Then he worked step by step until he was the best in the world.

cards.title: A kid on skis
cards.front: Jannik was born in 2001 in the Dolomite mountains of Italy.
cards.back: He started skiing at age 3. At 7, he won a national giant slalom title. He was one of Italy's top junior skiers.
cards.tryit: List three sports you've tried. Which one felt most fun?

cards.title: Choosing tennis at 13
cards.front: He played tennis, skiing and football as a kid.
cards.back: At 13 he picked tennis. He said in skiing, "if you make one mistake, then it's over." In tennis, you can fight back.
cards.tryit: Next match, after a lost point, take one breath and reset.

cards.title: Leaving home young
cards.front: At 13, he moved far from home to train.
cards.back: He went to Bordighera, Italy, to train with coach Riccardo Piatti. He thanks his parents for teaching him to be independent.
cards.tryit: Do one task by yourself today, like packing your tennis bag.

cards.title: Ski legs on court
cards.back: People think skiing helped his fast side-to-side moves. He hits hard from the baseline, like a Brawl Stars sharpshooter.
cards.tryit: Do 10 side-shuffles across the court, staying low and quick.

cards.title: Italy's first No. 1
cards.front: In June 2024, he became world No. 1.
cards.back: He was the first Italian ever to do it. By 2026 he'd won five Grand Slams and helped Italy win the Davis Cup twice.
cards.tryit: Write one tennis goal for this month and stick it on your wall.

quiz.q: What sport was Jannik a champion in as a young kid?
quiz.hint: Think about where he grew up: snowy mountains.
quiz.why: He won a national giant slalom ski title at just 7 years old.

quiz.q: Why did he like tennis more than ski racing?
opts: In tennis, one mistake doesn't end it
quiz.why: In a ski race one slip ends it, but in tennis you can win the next point.

quiz.q: How might skiing have helped his tennis?
opts: It helped his quick side-to-side moves
quiz.hint: Look at idea 4 about his legs.
quiz.why: Skiing trains balance and quick sideways movement, which helps on court.

quiz.q: What did Jannik become in June 2024?
quiz.why: He became the first Italian in history to be ranked world No. 1.

page.think: Jannik chose tennis because you can always fight back after a mistake. When you lose a point in a match, what helps you bounce back?
